config.title: Build request deduplication layer

intro.title: Build request deduplication layer
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a request deduplication layer, a component that prevents duplicate requests from being processed multiple times to improve efficiency and consistency in a Node.js application. You'll learn the core concept of using a cache or map to track ongoing requests, ensuring that identical requests wait for the first one to complete instead of executing again. The main technologies involved are JavaScript's built-in Map object for storing request promises and async/await for handling asynchronous operations. By the end, you'll have a functional deduplication layer that can be integrated into API handlers or data-fetching logic.
intro.usecase: Request deduplication is essential in Node.js backend systems where multiple clients might make identical API calls simultaneously. This pattern prevents redundant database queries or external API requests in scenarios like e-commerce product pages with concurrent user access, financial dashboard data refreshes, or real-time inventory management systems. By implementing a deduplication layer, developers optimize resource usage, reduce latency, and prevent rate-limiting issues when fetching user profiles, stock prices, or cached content. This technique is particularly valuable in microservices architectures where multiple services might request the same data from shared dependencies.

objectives: Construct a caching mechanism to store in-flight request promises
Implement a deduplication function that checks for duplicate requests before execution
Configure request parameters to serve as cache keys for deduplication
Integrate the deduplication layer with existing HTTP request functions
Manipulate cache entries to clear completed requests and prevent memory leaks
Initialize the deduplication system with configurable timeout settings
Apply the deduplication layer to batch identical API calls in a Node.js server

steps.title: Create request hash generation function
steps.instruction: Define a function named 'generateRequestHash' that takes 'method' and 'url' as parameters and returns an MD5 hash string using the crypto module.
steps.hint: Use crypto.createHash('md5') to create a hash object, then update it with the method and URL combined, and finally call digest('hex') to get the hexadecimal string.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function that generates a unique MD5 hash for each request based on its method and URL.
successCriteria: The 'generateRequestHash' function is defined, takes method and url parameters, uses crypto.createHash('md5'), updates with combined method and url, and returns a hexadecimal hash string.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your function uses crypto.createHash('md5'), updates with both method and URL, and returns the hexadecimal digest.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function isn't defined correctly. Remember to create a function named 'generateRequestHash' that takes method and url parameters and returns an MD5 hash using the crypto module.

steps.title: Implement deduplication middleware function
steps.instruction: Define a function named 'deduplicateRequest' that takes 'req' and 'res' as parameters and returns a promise. Inside the function, generate a request hash using the 'generateRequestHash' function and check if it exists in the 'requestCache' object.
steps.hint: Create a function that will handle deduplication logic. Use the existing 'generateRequestHash' function to create a unique key for each request, then check if that key already exists in the 'requestCache'.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named 'deduplicateRequest' is created that generates a request hash and checks the cache for duplicates, returning a promise.
successCriteria: The 'deduplicateRequest' function is defined with 'req' and 'res' parameters, calls 'generateRequestHash', checks 'requestCache', and returns a promise.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your function includes all the required elements: parameters, hash generation, cache check, and promise return.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function doesn't match the required structure. Review the instruction: create a function named 'deduplicateRequest' that takes req and res, generates a hash, checks the cache, and returns a promise.

steps.expectedOutcome: The simulateApiCall function is defined and ready to be used as a mock API endpoint in the server.

steps.title: Connect deduplication to simulated API
steps.instruction: Inside the deduplicateRequest function, call the simulateApiCall function for new requests (when the hash is not in cache) and store its result in the cache.
steps.hint: After checking if the hash exists in requestCache, if it doesn't, call simulateApiCall with the request object and assign its return value to the cache entry.
steps.expectedOutcome: The deduplicateRequest function will now properly call the simulated API for uncached requests and store the result in the cache.
successCriteria: The deduplicateRequest function calls simulateApiCall when a request hash is not found in requestCache and assigns the result to the cache.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.

steps.instruction: Modify the deduplicateRequest function to delete the cached request from requestCache once the simulated API call completes.

steps.expectedOutcome: The deduplicateRequest function will now automatically clean up completed requests from the cache to prevent memory leaks.
successCriteria: The deduplicateRequest function stores the promise in requestCache and removes it with .then() after resolution.

steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure to remove the hash from requestCache when the promise resolves.
